scriptSegments.narration: Nine critical vulnerabilities flashed red at NovaPay—and patching the 9.8 score first nearly cost ten million dollars.
Why? Because that 9.8 lived on an isolated cafeteria menu box holding zero customer data. Meanwhile, a 7.5 bug sat wide open on NovaPay's live ten-million-dollar payment checkout API.

CVSS measures technical severity, never business risk. Real CISOs prioritize using Likelihood times Business Impact, backed by Annualized Loss Expectancy: Single Loss Expectancy multiplied by Annual Rate of Occurrence. Spending $60K to eliminate a $4 million annual payment loss beats patching harmless 9.8s every time.
In 2013, Target suffered $292 million in breach costs after real payment-path threats drowned inside thousands of unprioritized security alerts.
You have $40K left and a risky legacy Fraud Engine costing $150K to rewrite. Mitigate, Transfer via Insurance, or Avoid? Vote now.
